findings.affected_surface: ruby_public_api - Time.parse is a public method in Ruby's standard library (lib/time.rb), part of the stable stdlib API.
findings.old_behavior: Time.parse accepts two arguments: date (String) and now (Time, defaults to self.now). The parsed timezone from the date string is passed directly to make_time as the zone parameter. If the date string has no timezone or offset, d[:zone] is nil and make_time treats the parsed time as local time. Passing an unknown keyword argument like zone: raises ArgumentError.
findings.new_behavior: Time.parse accepts an optional keyword argument zone: (defaults to nil). When the parsed date string does not include a time zone or offset (d[:zone] is nil), the zone: value is used as the fallback timezone. If zone: is provided and the date has no timezone, make_time receives the zone: value instead of nil, causing the parsed time to be interpreted in that zone rather than local time. If the date string already contains a timezone or offset, zone: is ignored (d[:zone] takes precedence via the || operator).
findings.compatibility_reason: The new zone: keyword argument relaxes the input contract: previously, passing zone: to Time.parse would raise ArgumentError (unknown keyword). Now it is accepted and used as a fallback timezone when the parsed date lacks a timezone. This is a backward-compatible additive change because: (1) existing callers without zone: continue to work identically (default nil makes d[:zone] || nil === d[:zone]), (2) existing callers with date strings that include a timezone or offset are unaffected (d[:zone] is truthy and takes precedence), and (3) the zone: argument only affects behavior when explicitly passed and the parsed date has no timezone. This enables easier migration from DateTime.parse (which defaults to UTC) to Time.parse.

evidence.snippet:
def parse(date, now=self.now, zone: nil)
      comp = !block_given?
      d = Date._parse(date, comp)
      year = d[:year]
      year = yield(year) if year && !comp
      make_time(date, year, d[:yday], d[:mon], d[:mday], d[:hour], d[:min], d[:sec], d[:sec_fraction], d[:zone] || zone, now)
    end

def parse(date, now=self.now)
      comp = !block_given?
      d = Date._parse(date, comp)
      year = d[:year]
      year = yield(year) if year && !comp
      make_time(date, year, d[:yday], d[:mon], d[:mday], d[:hour], d[:min], d[:sec], d[:sec_fraction], d[:zone], now)
    end

findings.why_not_internal_only: Time.parse is a public method on the Time class in Ruby's standard library (lib/time.rb). It is documented as a public API method and is widely used in Ruby applications. The change affects a public, documented API surface.
findings.uncertainty: Low. The diff is small and the behavioral change is clear: additive keyword argument with nil default. No existing call paths are affected. The only uncertainty is whether third-party code passing zone: (unlikely since it was invalid before) would have been catching ArgumentError from it.
findings.recommended_review: No manual review needed. The change is purely additive and backward compatible. If desired, verify that the documentation accurately describes the new parameter's behavior.
findings.test_recommendation: Verify backward compatibility: (1) existing calls without zone: produce identical results to before the patch, (2) existing calls with date strings that include timezone/offset are unaffected when zone: is also passed, (3) new zone: argument works correctly for dates without timezone, (4) passing zone: nil (explicitly) behaves same as not passing zone: at all.
